# `testing/no-large-snapshots`

**No inline snapshot longer than 50 lines**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Pack** | `@codelaw/rules-testing` (npm) |
| **Languages** | JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, TSX |
| **Turned on by** | no preset — name it in `[rules]` |
| **Severity when named without one** | `error` |
| **Options** | none — severity only |
| **Fix** | `manual` — no automatic fix; the steps are under *How to fix* (what to assert instead of the whole value is the author's choice) |
| **Stability** | `preview` — runs only with `preview = true` |
| **Since** | 0.5.0 |
| **Files** | only `**/*.test.*`, `**/*.spec.*`, `**/__tests__/**`, `**/test/**`, `**/tests/**`, `**/e2e/**` |
| **Ported from** | `eslint-plugin-jest/no-large-snapshots`, `@vitest/eslint-plugin/no-large-snapshots` |

## What it checks

An inline snapshot is at most 50 lines long. (The source's default; it also checks `.snap` files, which this rule does not read.)

**Why:** Nobody reviews a 200-line snapshot; it gets updated with `-u` whatever changed, and stops testing anything.

## Configuration

Everything below goes in `codelaw.toml` at the repo root. The same keys work as `[tool.codelaw]` in `pyproject.toml` or `"codelaw"` in `package.json` ([SR-CONFIG](../../../records/0110_config.md)).

### Turn it on

**Install the pack** (`codelaw init` does it for the languages it finds):

```bash
npm install --save-dev @codelaw/rules-testing
```

**No preset turns it on.** Load its pack through any preset (`codelaw:testing/jest` here), then name the rule in `[rules]`:

```toml
preview = true                        # pack rules are preview today
extends = ["codelaw:testing/jest"]

[rules]
"testing/no-large-snapshots" = "error"
```

- **A rule exists only once its pack is loaded** through `extends`; naming it in `[rules]` without that is an unknown rule id (exit 2).
- **Without `preview = true`** the rule is skipped and codelaw warns that it is preview.

### Severity

```toml
[rules]
"testing/no-large-snapshots" = "warn"    # error | warn | info | off
```

- **`error`** fails the run (exit 1) · **`warn`** fails only with `--max-warnings N` · **`info`** never fails · **`off`** turns it off.
- **Naming it with a severity turns it on** even when no preset does.

### For a group of files

A `[scope.<name>]` gives some files their own setting, applied after `[rules]` — the `tests` scope `codelaw:js/recommended` ships (`**/*.test.*`, `**/*.spec.*`); naming it extends it, so its files stay:

```toml
[scope.tests]
rules = { "testing/no-large-snapshots" = "off" }
```

A scope's `remap` changes whole severities in its files, after everything else: `remap = { error = "warn" }` never fails the run there.

### Warn locally, fail in CI

The `ci` profile runs when `CI` is set; `local` otherwise; `--profile <name>` or `CODELAW_PROFILE` picks one.

```toml
[profile.local.rules]
"testing/no-large-snapshots" = "warn"

[profile.ci.rules]
"testing/no-large-snapshots" = "error"
```

### In `pyproject.toml` or `package.json`

```toml
# pyproject.toml
[tool.codelaw.rules]
"testing/no-large-snapshots" = { severity = "warn" }
```

```json
{
  "codelaw": {
    "rules": {
      "testing/no-large-snapshots": {"severity": "warn"}
    }
  }
}
```

### Silence one finding

An inline `codelaw-ignore` always needs a reason; `expires=`, `warn_days=` and `by=` date it ([SR-LINTER](../../../records/0106_linter.md) decision 6).

- **JavaScript:** `// codelaw-ignore testing/no-large-snapshots: <reason>`
- **Dated:** `// codelaw-ignore testing/no-large-snapshots expires=2026-12-31 by=you@example.com: <reason>`

### Keep today's findings, fail on new ones

```bash
codelaw baseline add --rule testing/no-large-snapshots --expires 2026-12-31 --reason "<why>"
```

See [SR-BASELINE](../../../records/0104_baseline-and-deprecations.md).

### See what applies

```bash
codelaw explain testing/no-large-snapshots       # what it wants, why, how to fix
codelaw check --rule testing/no-large-snapshots  # only this rule
codelaw config --print --for <file>              # the resolved setting, and where it came from
```

## How to fix

1. Assert on the few fields the test is about (`toMatchObject`, `toHaveProperty`).
2. Or snapshot a smaller piece of the value.

## Examples

### JavaScript

#### Don't

```js
test("big", () => {
  expect(page).toMatchInlineSnapshot(`  line 0
  line 1
  line 2
  line 3
  line 4
  line 5
  line 6
  line 7
  line 8
  line 9
  line 10
  line 11
  line 12
  line 13
  line 14
  line 15
  line 16
  line 17
  line 18
  line 19
  line 20
  line 21
  line 22
  line 23
  line 24
  line 25
  line 26
  line 27
  line 28
  line 29
  line 30
  line 31
  line 32
  line 33
  line 34
  line 35
  line 36
  line 37
  line 38
  line 39
  line 40
  line 41
  line 42
  line 43
  line 44
  line 45
  line 46
  line 47
  line 48
  line 49
  line 50
  line 51
`);
});
```

#### Do

```js
test("big", () => {
  expect(page.title).toMatchInlineSnapshot(`"Home"`);
});
```
